Arif Cnr No.: Dlse-01-009183-2017 1. Sh. Razzaque Ahmed S/o Sh. Abdul Wahab R/o Rz-509, street no.25, Badi Masjid Tughlakabad-110019. ..........Petitioner Versus 1. Guru Dayal R/o Dd-726, Dabua Colony Nit Faridabad Haryana . ............Owner/Respondent no.2 Digitally signed by Charu Charu Gupta Gupta Date: 2025.08.26 17:06:07 +0530 Mact No.991/17 Razzaque v. Arif P.No. 1 Of 23 Bk 3. Iffco Tokio Insurance Company Ltd. Regd. Office: Iffco Sadan C-1, District Center Saket, New Delhi-110017. ............Insurance company/Respondent no.3 Date of accident : 01.07.2017 Result of accident : Grievous injury(Disability) Date of filing of Petition : 07.12.2017 Date of Decision : 26.08.2025 Award 1 . The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Razzaque Ahmed (39 years) suffered grievous injury and fracture in his right leg.
texts.facts: 1 . The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Razzaque Ahmed (39 years) suffered grievous injury and fracture in his right leg. An application u/s 166(1) MV Act was accordingly filed by the claimant/petitioner. Razzaque Ahmed vs Arif on 26 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69748430/ 1 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 01.07.2017 at about 04:30 p.m., petitioner/injured Razzaque alongwith his sister-in- law and his minor son were travelling from Bulandshar to Mirzapur on motorcycle bearing no.DL-3SCS-5600. When they reached near Mirzapur, U.P., a Maruti car bearing no.HR-51AB-8784(hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) came driven in rash and negligent manner from the opposite direction and hit the motorcycle from front right side. Due to the impact, all three riders on the bike fell and sustained injuries. Petitioner suffered a fracture in his right leg. He was taken to JPN Apex Trauma Center, AIIMs, New Delhi where he remained admitted till 09.07.2017. 3. An FIR no.1267/2017, dated 13.07.2017 was registered u/s 279/338 of IPC at PS Kotwali Dehat, Distt-Bulandshahr, U.P. Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.08.26 17:06:14 MACT NO.991/17 Razzaque v. Arif +0530 P.No. 2 Of 23 BK Matter was investigated and a chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court while claim petition was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is the driver, respondent no.2 is the owner and respondent no.3/Iffco Tokio Insurance company is the insurance company with which the offending vehicle was insured. 5. Despite service of notice, Respondent no.1 and 2 did not appear and were proceeded ex-parte vide order dated 16.04.2019. In its reply, respondent no.3 has refuted the occurrence of accident and doubted the claim for the reason of delay in lodging of the FIR. It has been pleaded that the insured was in breach of the conditions of policy in as much as the offending vehicle was entrusted for driving to Respondent no.1 who did not have a valid driving licence but only a temporary learner's licence. It has also been pleaded that since petitioner and other two injured were triple riding on the motorcycle without helmet, deduction qua contributory negligence be made. 6. Vide order dated 16.04.2019, following issues were framed. 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 01.07.2017 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. HR-51AB-8784 being driven by R1, owned by R2 and insured with R3? OPP 2. OPP. 3. Relief. 7. To prove his claim, petitioner Razzaque Ahmed led his Digitally signed by CHARU CHARU GUPTA Date: Razzaque Ahmed vs Arif on 26 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69748430/ 2 GUPTA 2025.08.26 17:06:21 +0530 MACT NO.991/17 Razzaque v. Arif P.No. 3 Of 23 BK evidence by examining himself as PW-1. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He testified on the lines of the claim petition and deposed that he sustained grievous injuries and was removed to Govt. hospital, Bulandshahr, U.P. from where he was referred to AIIMS Trauma center, Delhi. He was admitted on the date of accident i.e. 01.07.2017 and operated on 06.07.2017 during which a steel rod was inserted in his right leg. He was discharged on 09.07.2017. He took treatment for about six months. He further deposed that at the time of accident, he was working in Imagine Fashion at Tughlakabad Extension, Delhi as a Finishing Incharge and getting salary of Rs.24,500/- p.m. plus incentives. He spent Rs.1,50,000/- on his treatment, Rs.25,000/- on conveyance and Rs.30,000/- each on special diet and attendant. He relied upon copy of FIR as Mark-A, discharge summary as Ex.PW-1/2, medical bills as Ex.PW-1/3, pay slips as Ex.PW-1/4, Aadhar card as Mark-B, DL as Ex.PW-1/6, RC of offending vehicle as Mark-C, NCR of lost RC as Mark-D, insurance policy as Mark-E. He was duly cross - examined by Ld. counsel for insurance company/respondent no.3. After conclusion of petitioner evidence, insurance company led Respondent's evidence by examining Sh. Mrityunjay, Legal Executive of Iffco Tokio General Insurance company was examined as R-3W-1. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.R-3W-1/A. He relied upon documents i.e. Authority letter as Ex.R-3W-1/1, insurance policy as Ex.R-3W-1/2, learner's licence of driver as Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.08.26 Date: MACT NO.991/17 Razzaque v. Arif 17:06:27 +0530 P.No. 4 Of 23 BK Ex.R-3W-1/3, Notice u/O 12 Rule 8 CPC as Ex.R-3W-1/4 and postal receipts as Ex.R-3W-1/5. R-3W-1 was duly cross- examined.

He has categorically asserted that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by Respondent no.1. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 12. Further, driver of the offending vehicle has not challenged or denied by evidence, his rashness or negligence in driving of the offending vehicle or committing the accident. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
